Coordinators' Conclave-cum-Meeting of the Monitoring Committee for the First Year of Phase III (2025–30) under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative
articles.full_content:
The Coordinators' Conclave-cum-Meeting of the Monitoring Committee for the First Year of Phase III (2025–30) under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative was successfully organized by the CSIR-Human Resource Development Centre (CSIR-HRDC), Ghaziabad, in association with CSIR-National Chemical Laboratory (CSIR-NCL), Pune, on 06–07 August 2026 at CSIR-NCL, Pune. The two-day conclave served as a significant platform for reviewing the progress made during the first year of Phase III of the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative, facilitating knowledge exchange among participating laboratories, and strengthening collaborative efforts for the effective implementation of the programme.
The programme commenced with an inaugural session featuring the ceremonial welcome of dignitaries and participants, followed by the traditional lamp-lighting ceremony. Dr Rajesh G. Gonnade, Scientist-G, CSIR-NCL, welcomed the gathering and set the stage for the discussions by emphasizing the importance of collaboration, innovation and skill development in achieving the objectives of the meeting. Dr. Vinay Kumar, Scientist-G and Skill Nodal Principal Investigator, CSIR-HRDC, presented the objectives of the conclave and provided a brief overview of the remarkable progress achieved under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative during 2025–26. He highlighted the vision of CSIR integrated Skill Initiative’s pivotal role in creating a nationwide skill development ecosystem for nurturing industry-ready talent to build a technology-driven workforce. Dr. Abhishek Kumar, Scientist-F, CSIR-Central Planning Directorate (CPD) highlighted the significant achievements of the initiative and the policy interventions undertaken during the year. Dr. T. S. Rana, Head, CSIR-HRDC, Ghaziabad emphasized CSIR's commitment to transforming knowledge into digitally enabled, experiential, and innovation-driven solutions for skill development.
Dr. Mohana Krishna Reddy Mudiam, Director, Institute of Pesticide Formulation Technology (IPFT), Gurugram, and Chairman of the Monitoring Committee underscored that skill development is an integral part of nation-building and outlined five key priority pillars to guide the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative towards building a robust, future-ready, and industry-aligned skill development ecosystem. Dr. Ashish Lele, Director, CSIR-NCL, Pune emphasized that that CSIR is uniquely positioned to make a meaningful contribution to the Skill India Mission by leveraging its extensive nationwide laboratory network and scientific expertise to help position India as a global hub for skilled talent.
A major highlight of the conclave was the comprehensive review of the annual progress achieved during 2025–26 under Phase III of the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative. Throughout the first day, Skill Nodal Coordinators from all 37 participating CSIR laboratories presented their annual progress reports, highlighting the programmes conducted, trainee outreach, innovative initiatives, challenges en

CSIR-NIScPR Conducted Two-day Skill Training Program on “Popular Science Writing” and Motivated Participants to Communicate Science to Layman
articles.full_content:
New Delhi, 8 August 2026: CSIR-National Institute of Science Communication and Policy Research (NIScPR), New Delhi, successfully organised a two-day Skill Training Program on “Popular Science Writing” during 6–7 August 2026 under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative (Phase III). The program aimed to strengthen the science communication and writing skills of researchers, academicians, scientists, students, IT professionals, and R&D personnel. A total of 21 participants from across the country attended the Program.
Dr. Geetha Vani Rayasam, Director, CSIR-NIScPR addressing the participants of Popular Science Writing Traning Course
The Program was inaugurated by Dr. Geeta Vani Rayasam, Director, CSIR-NIScPR, who encouraged participants to communicate scientific research in a simple, accurate, and engaging manner to promote scientific temper and bridge the gap between science and society. Mr. Mukesh A. Pund, Head, Training Division, CSIR-NIScPR, welcomed the participants and highlighted the importance of popular science writing in enhancing the societal impact of scientific research. The Program was coordinated by Ms. Meetali Bharti, Nodal Principal Investigator, and Mr. Mohd. Salim Ansari, Co-Principal Investigator. Dr. Manish Mohan Gore, Course Coordinator, provided an overview of the Program and coordinated the academic sessions throughout the training.
The programme featured expert lectures and hands-on sessions delivered by eminent resource persons, including Ms. Neha Tripathi, who spoke on Basics of Popular Science Writing and Creative Formats; Dr. Bornali Sarma delivered a session on How to Write a Popular Science Story from a Research Article; Dr. Matiur Rahman discussed the Use of AI to Create Impactful Content for Social Media; NDTV’s Science Editor Shri Pallav Bagla, conducted a practical session on Science Writing for Digital Media; Dr. Meher Wan, Scientist-D explained the Skill of Writing Press Releases on Scientific Research and Events; and Dr. Manish Mohan Gore addressed the Ethical Aspects and Career Opportunities in Popular Science Writing. The program also included interactive discussions and hands-on exercises on various genres of popular science writing, enabling participants to gain practical experience in communicating science effectively. Participants appreciated the program's practical orientation and the opportunity to interact with experienced science communicators and media professionals. The training enhanced their understanding of effective science communication, digital content creation, and science writing for diverse audiences.
The Program concluded with a valedictory session, during which Mr. Mukesh A. Pund, Head, Training addressed the participants and distributed certificates with the Program Team members. The successful completion of the program reaffirmed CSIR-NIScPR's commitment to developing skilled science communicators and promoting excellence in science communication through capacity-building initiatives under

The program aimed to strengthen the science communication and writing skills of researchers, academicians, scientists, students, IT professionals, and R&D personnel.
